trajectory.development: Book 24 is the review point of the Special Draw Right, recorded in the Working Book as agent-proposed (E10). The Right is conditional on training apprentices from outside the lineage, and the lineage needs that condition shown or the Right is exposed (E4). The labour gap is first met by people rather than by a schedule, and the Book exports a public capability record separate from debt, tally and aggregate balance (E8).
trajectory.becomes_available: Makes possible a review of the Right by people who have never seen the labour done, since a generation that came of age after Book 20 has only known lineage crews performing it under the Right (E9).
trajectory.changes: The Right stops being a standing exemption and becomes a practice whose training condition must be shown, so the lineage's concern about dilution (E4) becomes a test rather than an assumption.

trajectory.development: Oona Brisk and the Mill Compact offer hired lowland labour if it is credited against the Compact's draw. The offer is neither accepted nor refused, because the Compact's settlement is author-reserved (E5). The remnant's custody offer is declined while Oona's offer stands (E13).
trajectory.becomes_available: Once Book 24 has made the labour gap a matter for people, an outside offer to meet it becomes a live choice. Under condition B the Compact's purchased draw would owe grain-labour to the rebuild (E24), although that draw is recorded as carrying no return labour (E2).
trajectory.changes: Crediting hired hands against the draw would move return labour onto purchased shares that are recorded as carrying none (E2), and would give the lineage Right a second source of labour to weigh against it.

trajectory.development: The Mill Compact's own bid, which the record places in Books 27 to 29 (E2). Oona's standing offer meets a valley with some hands of its own before that bid (E12).
trajectory.becomes_available: Once the valley's own hands have been tested under the Right and the credit question has been answered, the bid can be read against what the valley actually did with its repair capability (E12).
trajectory.changes: The bid's meaning depends on the Book 24 outcome: a valley that accepted or declined outside labour meets the bid on different terms, and settlement of the draw stays author-reserved (E5).

trajectory.development: If the public capability record exported in Book 24 (E8) is later used to register who can repair, whatever their origin, a later Book could show lineage labour and any credited hired labour in one record, with the purchased draw kept apart from return labour as an option.
trajectory.becomes_available: Requires the Book 24 record to exist and the Compact's draw settlement to be decided, since whether the draw is kept apart from return labour depends on condition B (E24) and on the settlement (E5).
trajectory.changes: Credited labour would enter the rebuild as demonstrated capability rather than as purchased draw, testing whether the Right's training condition and the Compact's offer can share one account of who repairs.

relations.reason: Under condition B the purchased draw owes grain-labour to the rebuild (E24), but the Compact's draw is recorded as carrying no return labour (E2). If B holds, the Compact's shares join the labour the Right carries, so the two accounts of who owes labour meet. Condition B is not defined in the supplied record.

Whether hired lowland labour (E5) can count toward the Right's condition of training outside apprentices (E10) is contested by the lineage's fear of dilution by untrained gift-hands (E4, an agent inference). The offer and the Right pull against each other on what counts as trained hands.

The record places the valley's own hands before the Compact's bid (E12). Lineage training of outside apprentices would help the valley take Compact labour without dilution, but nothing recorded makes that training necessary for the bid itself.

The supplied record does not make the Compact's settlement depend on the Right's review, and the settlement is author-reserved (E5). Only the early-bid path changes the order in which the two arrive (E6).

alternative_paths.ordering: Oona's bid is brought forward, ahead of the Right's Book 24 review.
alternative_paths.effect: Hired labour arrives before the training condition is shown, so the Right is reviewed against an outside offer already on the table. The bid would displace Books 27 to 29 and press on the author-reserved settlement (E6).

alternative_paths.ordering: The Right's training condition is demonstrated in Book 24 before any Compact labour is credited against the draw.
alternative_paths.effect: Credited hands then arrive as demonstrated trained hands, which answers the lineage's dilution concern (E4). The draw takes on rebuild labour only after the Right has been shown to hold.

alternative_paths.ordering: Condition B is not reached, and the Compact joins only at its Books 27 to 29 bid.
alternative_paths.effect: Lineage crews and households that meet the rota carry the rebuild alone through Book 24 (E1), while the training condition stays unshown (E4), so the Right stays exposed for longer.

opportunities.text: Inferred: if credited hired lowland hands are trained as apprentices, they could meet the Right's condition of outside training, so the condition could be demonstrated rather than left exposed. Dilution concerns would then be answered by a training standard, not only by refusal.

Inferred: crediting the Compact's labour against its draw (E5) would bring the purchased draw under the rebuild that the lineage Right now carries (E24). Return labour could then be shared rather than borne by lineage crews and by households that can meet the rota, which is the cost E1 names for families with few hands.

Inferred: the public capability record exported in Book 24 (E8) could register who can repair regardless of origin, separate from debt and tally. Counted and uncounted practice (E7) could then both be recognised without the Compact's debt and trade logic absorbing the labour (E2).

reader_experience: The reader first meets the lineage repair as a practice others carry quietly, then sees the cost surface when Book 24 asks people to give back the water before it is owed. The Compact's offer leaves a live choice open between accepting outside hands and proving the Right, with no answer yet. Book 24 stands on its own as the review and the first capability record without the settlement resolved, and the offer stays open rather than refused, which the reader should feel as a choice still in play.
open_decisions: Whether Oona's hired lowland labour may be credited against the Compact's draw, a question the record reserves to the author's settlement (E5).
Whether the Right's training condition can be met by credited hired hands, or only by apprentices trained from outside the lineage (E10).
What condition B is, since the link under which purchased draw owes grain-labour has no definition in the supplied record (E24).
Which body, if any, would grant the cohort standing in coordinating channel work; Book 24 names none and creates none (E11).
uncertainty: Books 24 and 25 carry identical text for all nine elements listed (E23). This reading places stages in Book 24 and cannot tell whether Book 25 adds a distinct development.
The Book 24 review point and the training condition are agent-proposed, and the source gives a reversal the request does not state (E10, E4). The Right may not reach Book 24 as described.
The excerpts of E3 and E8 are truncated, so the author's full vision and the full Book 24 exercise were not read in full.
Condition B and the Compact's settlement are undefined or reserved, so the complication in the relations is conditional and not established as fact (E2, E24).
